course_name_original: Tecnologías de unión: soldadura y adhesivos (18440)

learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of materials science and engineering.
Have adequate knowledge of materials science and engineering, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field in mechanical engineering.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve materials science and engineering problems using established methods.
Be able to design and conduct materials science and engineering experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory skills in materials science and engineering.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
An adequate knowledge of their engineering branch that includes some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.

syllabus_topics: Non-destructive testing. Visual inspection. Acoustic inspection. Penetrant liquids. Magnetic particles. Induction currents: Eddy currents. Radiography and gamma radiography. Ultrasonics. Active thermography. Holographic interferometry. Test selection.

Welding technology. Materials to be welded. Fe-C system and heat treatments of steels. Aluminum-based alloys hardened by aging or deformation. Types of welding. Fusion welding. Non-fusion welding. Heat flow. Mass flow. Gases.
Welding metallurgy. Solidification of the weld pool. Transformations in the Fe-C system. Alloys hardened by aging or maturation. Alloys hardened by deformation. Galvanized steel sheet. Defectology.

Introduction to adhesives. Basic concepts of adhesion. Formation of the adhesive joint. Design criteria and examples. Comparison of joining techniques. The interface. Adhesion models (mechanical, chemical bond, electrical, diffusion). Effect of weak preferential fracture layers.
Surface treatments. Surface characteristics: Roughness. Influencing factors. Pre-treatments: Abrasion and cleaning. Chemical treatments. Physical treatments. Surface analysis techniques.

Mechanical behavior and degradation. Mechanical properties of polymer materials. Mechanical stresses of the adhesive joint. Analysis of simple lap joints. Fracture mechanics. Degradation. Effect of temperature, humidity, and solvents. Mechanical and thermal fatigue. Combined effects.

Families of adhesives. Polymerization process. Families of adhesives. Dosing systems. Rigid adhesives: Epoxy, Cyanoacrylates, Anaerobics, and Acrylics. Flexible adhesives: Polysulfides, Silicones, Polyurethanes, and Modified Silanes. Pre-polymerized adhesives: liquid phase, adhesive tapes, and hot melts.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (written documentation and oral presentation of work)

assessment_rules: The continuous assessment accounts for 40% of the final grade and involves preparing written documentation and an oral presentation of at least one work. The final ordinary exam accounts for the remaining 60% of the grade, and it is necessary to pass this exam with a grade of 4 or higher for it to be weighted with the continuous assessment. A final overall grade of 5 is required to pass the course. The extraordinary exam counts for 60% if continuous assessment is considered, or 100% if continuous assessment is not considered.
